title: Tesserae hardware catalog entry
description: A data-only SKU definition that derives a device kind from an existing protocol-level device folder. The hardware entry brings identity (name, vendor, url), panel specifics (dims, gamut, native stride), and optional protocol-specific defaults; the referenced protocol contributes the wire-format implementation (parse_status, validate_config, status/config topics).

tesserae_compat.description: Host major-version compatibility, same convention as device.json.

id.description: Unique kind id for this SKU. Used in URLs, device-instance kind_of references, and the compatibility matrix. Cannot collide with an existing devices/<id>/ folder; folder always wins on conflict.

icon.description: Phosphor icon slug (no 'ph-' prefix). Falls back to the protocol's icon when absent.

protocol.description: Id of the protocol-level device folder under devices/ whose Python module supplies parse_status / validate_config and whose manifest contributes status_topic / config_topic / renderers / config_schema defaults. Validated at load time against the registry.

panel.description: Physical panel for this SKU. Replaces the protocol's default panel block wholesale; native_w/native_h are forwarded to renderers that pack at firmware stride.

gamut.description: Panel colour gamut id (e.g. 'waveshare_e6'/'spectra_6', 'inky_7colour'/'acep_7colour', 'bwry_4', 'bwr_3', 'gray_4', 'gray_16', 'mono'). Colour gamuts are read by the quantizer when packing the .bin buffer; grayscale/mono ids are metadata for the renderer and colour-capability surfaces.

col_offset.description: Hidden-column padding inside the native buffer: x-offset of the first visible column. Only meaningful alongside native_w/native_h wider than the visible w; when present the .bin packers pad the frame with white instead of scaling to the native width (Seeed 2.13" BWRY: 122 visible in a 128-wide JD79676 buffer, col_offset 6).

protocol_config.description: Free-form protocol-specific defaults. Each protocol decides what's meaningful here (e.g. TRMNL BYOS reads 'model_header' to drive auto-provisioning; MQTT bin pushers read 'image_format'). Validation is the protocol's responsibility, not this schema's.

config_schema_extends.description: Optional additions to the protocol's config_schema, merged additively over the protocol's defaults. Same shape as device.json config_schema. Use sparingly; most SKUs should inherit the protocol's form as-is.

refresh_floor_s.description: Lower bound on the device's poll cadence in seconds. Surfaced in the Settings UI so the user can't set a smaller refresh_rate than the panel actually supports.

image_format.description: Wire format this SKU expects. Informational; the protocol's renderers still drive the actual encoding.

touch.description: Whether this SKU's panel has a digitizer. A hardware fact, distinct from the firmware's touch_enabled config. Set true and Tesserae's touch dispatch and the editors' Interaction UI apply to the panel, and the device APIs report it so agents and the editor know it is tappable. Absent → not tappable.

renderers.description: Optional override for the protocol's default renderer list. Present when the same wire protocol serves panels with meaningfully different output formats, e.g. a colour Spectra 6 panel wants an indexed-palette PNG while the mono panels on the same protocol take 1-bit output. Absent → inherit the protocol's renderers verbatim (the common case).

notes_md.description: Free-form maintainer notes in markdown. Surfaced on the docs hardware page.

auto_select.description: Whether a device's self-report may be resolved to this SKU automatically (relay pairing infers the most specific kind from the reported protocol + gamut). Set false for a variant that is indistinguishable on the wire from a sibling SKU and differs only in which firmware image was flashed: nothing the device sends can identify it, so guessing risks pinning the panel to the wrong OTA lineage. Such a kind is only ever set explicitly by the operator, or by the firmware declaring it at register / discover.

deprecated_aliases.description: Older kind ids this SKU also registers under, so device instances created against the old id keep resolving. Only add when actually renaming a previously-shipped kind.
